release_slices.name: Storefront checkout cart preservation hotfix
release_slices.plain_english_purpose: Keep an eligible tenant-store order and its totals in checkout for both guests and signed-in DGFY customers when an unrelated service-booking capability is unavailable.
release_slices.purpose: Keep an eligible tenant-store order and its totals in checkout for both guests and signed-in DGFY customers when an unrelated service-booking capability is unavailable.
release_slices.implementation_summary: Replaces the Storefront cart cleanup rule that required product cart, checkout, and service booking capabilities simultaneously with line-type-aware cleanup. Product lines require product-cart and checkout capability; service lines require booking capability. Existing guest drafts, DGFY auth resume, quote, stock, payment, tenant, and order submission contracts remain unchanged.
included_features: Capability-aware preservation of product checkout carts
Independent fail-closed handling for service booking carts
Guest and DGFY-account regression coverage for the tenant-store checkout condition
excluded_features: Payment routing, PayMongo, QR Ph, billing, settlement, or fee changes
Tenant authorization or DGFY membership changes
Catalog, stock, quote, price, fulfillment, or order-submission API changes
Unrelated local inventory, CSV import, error-handler, and POS work
release_slices.owner_attribution: BabyBaBab owner-authorized hotfix and production deployment
release_slices.regression_warning_summary: The hotfix changes when Storefront cart state is discarded. A regression could retain a cart after its relevant checkout capability is revoked or still erase a valid cart during guest or DGFY-account checkout.
potentially_affected_existing_behaviors: Tenant-store product cart retention during checkout
evidence_covering_regression_risk: Unit tests cover guest and DGFY-account product carts when booking is unavailable, product checkout revocation, service booking preservation, and service booking revocation.
PR #51 CI passed the full backend matrix, full frontend suite, all frontend app builds, bundle budgets, architecture, compliance, docs, dependency, merge-adoption, and batch-inventory gates.
Live pre-deploy Eatery ni Doe guest checkout retained Kare-kare, PHP 70.70 total, and promo entry through payment review without submitting an order.
Backend DGFY/store-auth fallback tests passed and continued to require explicit DGFY linkage rather than email matching.
evidence_gaps: A controlled signed-in DGFY production checkout-resume smoke still requires the dedicated production UAT account and must be completed after deployment.

The live tenant currently advertises booking capability as enabled, so post-deploy production proof must supplement the real tenant journey with exact-bundle source proof for the booking-disabled branch.
rollback_or_monitoring_notes: Rollback by reverting the hotfix and release-evidence commits, rebuilding Storefront, and redeploying through the signed controller.
Monitor Storefront quote failures, empty-cart checkout states, DGFY auth-resume failures, guest draft restoration errors, and checkout validation errors after deployment.

documentation_closure.rationale: The implementation stays within the existing Storefront customer-access boundary and does not change architecture or API contracts. Release documentation is updated because this is a high-risk customer-flow hotfix requiring explicit adoption, regression, rollback, and production-accuracy evidence.

documents.evidence: Records the exact preserved Storefront behaviors, changed source anchors, tests, rendered proof, and production proof required for PR #51.
Provides the reviewed batch inventory, regression warning, completed test evidence, rollback, and production accuracy requirements for this exact hotfix slice.

release_slices.adr_or_compliance: No ADR or compliance declaration is required because the fix stays within the accepted Storefront customer-access boundary and changes no payment, persistence, authorization, or compliance contract.
release_slices.rollback_notes: Revert the checkout hotfix and its release evidence as one release slice, rebuild all frontend apps, rerun frontend, architecture, compliance, docs, merge-adoption, and regression-risk gates, then redeploy through the signed controller.
